issue: Is a semiautomatic firearm fitted with a bump stock a "machinegun" under the National Firearms Act's definition, so that the Bureau's rule banning bump stocks is lawful?

sides.position: A firearm fitted with a bump stock is not a machinegun, so the Act does not let the Bureau ban bump stocks.
cases: Cargill v. Garland, 57 F.4th 447 (5th Cir. 2023) (en banc)
Hardin v. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, 2023 WL 3065807 (6th Cir. 2023)

sides.position: A firearm fitted with a bump stock is a machinegun, so the Bureau's rule banning bump stocks is a valid reading of the Act.
cases: Guedes v. ATF, 45 F.4th 310 (D.C. Cir. 2022) (Guedes II)
Guedes v. ATF, No. 21-5045 (D.C. Cir. 2023) (order denying reh'g en banc)

this_court: upholds the Bureau's rule: bump-stocked firearms are machineguns (Guedes II)
quote: Here, circuits are split on the best reading of the National Firearms Act’s definition of “machinegun.”
cite: Damien Guedes v. ATF (ORDER IN SLIP OPINION FORMAT), No. 21-5045 (D.C. Cir. 2023)
